title: Whole congregation should sing
summary: She argues everyone in church should sing, clap and take part, not only the choir.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, I'll say this. This new world we are living in is tired of putting on a farm. People wants to live. People wants to enjoy life. And they don't want to go to church and set up and not be a part of the service. I think a whole church should sing, not just the choir. Let everybody sing their song. No care whether it sounds good or bad, that's their song. And they'll feel good trying to sing their song.
I think that's a wonderful idea that we could all be part of.

Do it yourself. Get out and sing yourself. Clap your hands yourself. Dance yourself. And you'll feel better. Don't you? You're right. Sure, I think so. All this informal stuff of you going to church, sitting there, just listening. Be a part of that thing and you can know how glorious it is what you're receiving. That's what I think.
